How was your gig?

So very awesome, thanks for asking. Being called out onto the stage to a cheering and yelling crowd is a huge ego boost. I gave a pretty good performance, f I do say so myself. I should have soundboard recordings later this week, so if they are good ill share them.

At the end of the guitar thread, I wrote about the experience in more detail. It was fantastic! Thanks for asking!

It really is such an honor to be able to play for them. For those too short hours, they give me permission to control how they emote, how they move, and how they think. I can give them new memories and remind them of old memories. I can make them dance, laugh, cry, and smile. It truly is an honor and I'm very much a professional. They paid money to see me and it's my job to ensure it was a good investment for them to make.

I'm going to do it again soon. In just a few short weeks, they're playing a much larger crowd and I've been invited to join them. I pretty much have an open invitation. I like to tell myself it's because I'm good, but it's probably 'cause I'm free. ;-)

Anyhow, I even did a solo piece and sang. I don't do that much, as I prefer to just play. But, they egged me on and I'd brought two electrics and an acoustic with me, so I busted out Tears in Heaven for them. They slow danced, bodies more or less in time, and the rest of the band took that time to get a longer break.

I called my son on for the encore. We were playing Free Bird and he knows the song. We've also played it together a lot, so we can be pretty fancy. We can reach across and play each other's guitar which made the crowd go nuts. It's much easier than it looks like but I don't get to play with my son often, and even less on stage.

There were about 800 people, I guess. Not a bad crowd and they were way too good to me. It brought back a lot of memories and I do miss performing. I just don't miss it enough to go back to doing it every weekend. It's nice not doing it for money, but doing it for passion. I truly enjoyed my job, and it is a job. My job is to make it a night they'll remember and want to do again. Really, my job is to make them buy drinks and want to come back to that specific bar, or go to bars where the band is playing. It is work, a profession. That doesn't mean it can't be impassioned or that it has to be boring. It's a labor of love.

That's the short version. I could probably write 10,000 words about it. It was great. My daughter left the following day. My son is still here and will probably go play with us the next time I go - assuming he practices. He could have been a better guitarist than I. He's got some quick and accurate fingers. I had him taking formal lessons at an early age. He's just not been practicing very much.

Thanks for asking! I love to share my experiences with other people and enjoy writing, even if just on a tablet.
